title: Make a local commit
summary: A commit records the staged snapshot with a message. Git needs a name and email label, which are part of the commit metadata.
introduction: A commit records the staged snapshot with a message. Git needs a name and email label, which are part of the commit metadata. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A commit records the staged snapshot with a message. Git needs a name and email label, which are part of the commit metadata.

blocks.code:
git config user.name "Practice Learner"
git config user.email "learner@example.test"
git commit -m "Add first practice note"
blocks.title: Make a local commit

blocks.text: The local repository records the staged note. These labels are for this practice repository, not a login.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a message describing one clear change in your own words.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Real published commits expose their author metadata; do not use personal details carelessly.
For more detail later, use this [Git further reading](https://git-scm.com/docs/gittutorial).

seo.title: Git: Make a local commit
seo.description: Learn about make a local commit in Git. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
